correctness.rationale: For every nonnegative real m by (d+1) matrix without zero rows and d,m>=1, projection of any Euclidean ball onto the standard d-simplex bounds its radius by 1/(d+sqrt(d)), with unique projected center at equality. At that center, fiber lower and upper halfspaces impose independent intervals rho<=x_i<=rho(B_i-H_i); these exist iff B_i>=1+H_i for every row. Containment in all defining halfspaces proves sufficiency. For positive integral entries the contained product simplex times unit cube proves strictness when d>=2. In Ferroni sparse A, B and H are explicitly calculated, and (B-1)^2-H^2=2[alpha sqrt(d)(beta-1)+beta(alpha-1)] proves exactly one degenerate parameter pair. Contact facets correspond to saturated center-coordinate bounds. Standalone verifier reported 1,120 independent numerical LPs and 19,865 successful assertions; finite checks only corroborate the analytic proof.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite-dimensional Cayley-polytope family highlighted by a new 2026 source, the result resolves a sharp structural metric question: exactly which arbitrary nonnegative box width matrices allow the maximum possible projected-simplex radius, and precisely what are ALL centers and contacting facets. Entrywise-positive integer matrices (known to define smooth polytopes) have identical inradius independent of matrix sizes while retaining a full fiber-dimensional family of centers; the sparse alpha,beta family has an exceptional unique center and otherwise a cube of optimal centers. These are motivated complete classifications and extremal-equality regimes rather than a small numerical increment or table recomputation.
